monitor.title: Signal Monitor
monitor.subtitle: Each strategy source keeps its own watchlist and scan results. The three boxes are CSI 300: last few days, positioning, and “is this a bear market?” Soft-bear means do not buy new names today — not a bear-market call.
monitor.symbolsHint: Up to 20 tickers, comma-separated; stored per strategy source. Watchlist alerts only; holdings use the full run universe.
monitor.strategyHint: Only backtests with signal_engine.py are listed; chat-only runs are omitted. Switching loads that run’s symbols and last scan.
monitor.strategyNoPrompt: No prompt recorded for this run.
monitor.strategyNoCode: No signal_engine.py found for this run.
monitor.maintainRunsHint: Rename titles to make the picker easier to scan, or delete unused backtest runs. Deletes cannot be undone.
monitor.deleteRunDesc: Permanently removes the run directory plus its monitor board and scan history.
monitor.scheduleHint: 5-field cron in UTC (no ranges), e.g. 30 7 * * * ≈ 15:30 CST daily.
monitor.refreshReportHint: When checked, re-run the bound backtest through today so K-lines and buy/sell markers on the strategy report update. Slower on large universes.
monitor.resetHistoryDesc: Deletes all holdings snapshots for this strategy and rescans from today as day one (current names count as enters). Watchlist and strategy source are kept.
monitor.emptySuggestions: No suggestions yet. Save symbols for this strategy source and click Scan now.
monitor.holdingsHint: Strategy target weights (not broker positions). Full-universe weights; same-day rescans always rebase on the prior holdings day and recalculate live.
monitor.emptyHoldings: No holdings yet. After a scan, names with weight > 0 appear here.
monitor.opsEmpty: No day-over-day ops yet (first scan or unchanged book).
monitor.historyHint: Pick a date to replay that day’s holdings and ops.
monitor.provisionalHint: Uses live price as today’s close proxy; may flip after the official close.
monitor.discussPrompt: Explain the {{action}} suggestion for {{symbol}} (current position: {{position}}): {{reason}}. Keep it concise and actionable.
monitor.forecastHint: Projects 10-session up and down paths from historical look-alikes, with MA5/MA10/MA20. Statistical scenarios only — not a price target or investment advice. Hover probs, tape actions, and market/veto labels for term glosses.
monitor.forecastEmpty: No active holdings to evaluate. Scan first so target weights appear.
monitor.forecastCapped: Showing the top {{count}} holdings by weight.
monitor.forecastBiasUp: Book tilt: higher odds of a 10-day rise
monitor.forecastBiasDown: Book tilt: higher odds of a 10-day decline
monitor.forecastBiasNeutral: Book tilt: up and down odds are close
monitor.forecastBiasAbstained: Book tilt: confidence too low — read the scenario paths only
monitor.forecastMarketIdle: CSI 300 has no strong signal — stock analog stands
monitor.forecastMarketConfirm: agrees with the strong CSI 300 analog
monitor.forecastVetoDisagree: vetoed: disagrees with a strong CSI 300 analog
monitor.forecastVetoAbstained: legacy save: CSI 300 did not call
monitor.forecastHistoryHint: Pick a time to replay that saved report. It does not refetch market data.
monitor.forecastTrendChop: CSI 300 is range-bound: buy dips, sell highs. Hold a name that itself is in an uptrend.
monitor.forecastTrendBull: CSI 300 medium uptrend: do not add this book
monitor.forecastTrendBear: CSI 300 medium soft-bear: do not buy new names today (not a 5-day call, not a bear market)
monitor.horizonStripTitle: How to read CSI 300 (long only — you cannot short)
monitor.horizonMeaningShortBull: Recent days are firm; they do not size the book
monitor.horizonMeaningShortChop: The last few days are mixed — not a sizing call
monitor.horizonMeaningShortBear: Recent days are weak; that alone does not flatten
monitor.horizonMeaningMediumBull: Index is up; still do not add this theme
monitor.horizonMeaningMediumChop: Buy dips / sell highs in names
monitor.horizonMeaningMediumBear: Do not buy new names today
monitor.horizonMeaningLongBull: Price is above the year line
monitor.horizonMeaningLongChop: Year line intact — not a bear market
monitor.horizonMeaningLongBear: Below the year line, still not a bear-market verdict
monitor.horizonHeadlineMediumLongBear: Medium is soft-bear, so do not buy new names today. Long soft-bear only means the year line is broken — not that a bear market is confirmed.
monitor.horizonHeadlineMediumBear: Medium is soft-bear: no new buys today. The year line is not broken, so this is not a bear market; keep or trim what you already hold.
monitor.horizonHeadlineMediumBull: The index is in a medium uptrend, but that historically does not lift this theme — still no adds.
monitor.horizonHeadlineShortBearChop: Only the last few days are weak. Sizing follows the middle box, which is still range-bound: buy dips, do not flatten.
monitor.horizonHeadlineChop: Range is the default. Buy dips and sell highs in names. A real soft-bear needs a down-stacked tape and a negative half-year return.
monitor.horizonHowToMediumLongBear: To flip back: a close above the 60-day line ends the medium soft-bear; a close above the year line ends the long one. A classic bear market usually also needs ~20% off the peak.
monitor.horizonHowToMediumBear: A close back above the 60-day line returns medium to range. While the year line holds, 0% means no new buys — not a broker flatten.
monitor.horizonHowToMediumBull: Short-term strength or weakness only explains the last few days; it does not change “do not add this theme.”
monitor.horizonHowToShortBearChop: Short-term flip: close back above the 5-day line. Sizing still follows the middle box.
monitor.horizonHowToChop: A real soft-bear needs the 20/60/120-day averages stacked down, a close under the 60-day line, and a negative half-year return.
monitor.horizonMediumDrives: Sizing follows the middle box. The last few days only explain noise; the right box asks if this is a bear market. Wait / 0% = no new buys today, not a broker flatten.
monitor.hintHorizonShort: 5/10/20-day averages. A two-day drop is short-term weakness. It does not zero the book by itself.
monitor.hintHorizonMedium: Roughly 1–6 months. This is the shared add gate: soft-bear = do not buy new names today.
monitor.hintHorizonLong: Close vs the year line. Breaking it is a caution, not “bear market confirmed.” A classic bear usually also needs ~20% off the peak.
monitor.colTrendActionHint: Long-only dual-track tape (MA20/60/120): Hold = relative strength, buy-dip / sell-rally = range edges, Reduce = knife. Separate from strategy enter/trim and from 10-day up/down colors.
monitor.hintHold: Relative strength: index chop + the name’s own bull stack. The cell that historically continued — not chasing an index bull.
monitor.hintBuyDip: Buy the dip: index chop, stock not bear, close in the bottom ~20% of the 60-day range. Long-only cheap entry.
monitor.hintSellRally: Sell the rally: close in the top ~20% of the 60-day range, or a bounce in an index bear. Not a short.
monitor.hintReduce: Knife: stock bear stack (in chop or when the name lags an index bull). Down-continuation side — cut / do not add; not a catch.
monitor.hintWait: Wait / no add: mid-range, or not an add environment (e.g. index bull for this book). Do not chase.
monitor.hintTrendChop: Index chop is the default buy-low / sell-high regime; a name with its own bull stack gets Hold (RS).
monitor.hintTrendBull: Index bull does not lift this book — no adds. The 10-day analog is only a short-horizon reverse veto, not a chase signal.
monitor.hintTrendBear: Medium soft-bear = do not buy new names in this theme today. Not a two-day down-day verdict, and not a bear-market call. Suggested size 0% is today’s no-add cap, not a broker flatten. Retail accounts cannot short.
monitor.hintBiasUp: Book-level: among called names, weight tilts toward a higher 10-day up probability. Not every name is bullish.
monitor.hintBiasDown: Book-level: among called names, weight tilts toward a higher 10-day down probability. Not every name is bearish.
monitor.hintBiasNeutral: Book-level odds are close, or too few names were called — read each scenario band.
monitor.hintBiasAbstained: Almost no name cleared the confidence bar; paths only, no book direction.
monitor.hintMarketDecisive: CSI 300 analog is one-sided and large enough to act as a strong barometer. It only clears a stock call when it disagrees.
monitor.hintMarketIdle: CSI 300 is weak or two-sided: no veto; stock analogs stand.
monitor.hintMarketConfirm: Stock call agrees with a strong CSI 300 barometer. Not required; a weak index never blocks a stock.
monitor.hintVetoDisagree: Strong opposite CSI 300: clears this name’s directional call (probs go muted). Scenario K paths stay.
monitor.hintVetoAbstained: Legacy save wording: index was not decisive then. Current rules do not veto on a weak index.
monitor.hintAbstained: Style / confidence / margin not met: scenario bands only, no colored directional call.
monitor.hintProbCalled: Softmax neighbor vote for up vs down scenarios. Color means a formal call (lopsided + style). Not an expected return %.
monitor.hintProbMuted: Still the analog vote probabilities, but no formal call (low confidence or market veto) — shown muted.
monitor.hintStyle: Does history rhyme: mean neighbor similarity × nearest-neighbor percentile. Too low → no call.
monitor.hintConfidence: How lopsided the vote is × style. Needs style and probability margin too before coloring.
monitor.hintAnalogs: Count of de-overlapped historical look-alikes, and how many printed up vs down over the next 10 days.
monitor.hintStockBull: Stock MA20>MA60>MA120, price above MA60, +120d momentum. In chop this often maps to Hold (RS).
monitor.hintStockChop: Stock MAs are not a clean bull or bear stack.
monitor.hintStockBear: Stock bear stack with negative 120d momentum. Often maps to Reduce (knife).
monitor.hintSwingOversold: Close in the bottom ~20% of the 60-day range — buy-dip territory in chop.
monitor.hintSwingMid: Mid-range close — usually wait until cheap or the name turns bull.
monitor.hintSwingOverbought: Close in the top ~20% of the 60-day range — sell-rally territory.
monitor.hintRsShare: RS share: fraction of names whose own MA stack is bull. Index bear still shows this map; it is not a hold recommendation.
monitor.hintKnifeShare: Knife share: fraction of names whose own MA stack is bear. Higher ≈ more knives. Index bear still shows this map.

marketPick.title: Market Pick
marketPick.subtitle: Screen Eastmoney industry and concept boards with the dual-track tape (relative strength vs knife). Boards below their own EW/MA20, or whose bound strategy book is empty, stay on the table and are not the pick. Index bull does not mean chase a theme. Boards with a researched recipe can be tracked on Sector Pick.
marketPick.alreadyScanned: Today's snapshot already exists. Click Refresh today again to rebuild it.
marketPick.emptyHero: No snapshot yet. Click Refresh today — this page never auto-scans on open.
marketPick.noPickHint: Display only. Do not open a new theme book.
marketPick.historyHint: Pick a date to replay that day’s recommended board and ranking. Same-day refreshes keep only the latest pass.
marketPick.disclaimer: This screen does not run SignalEngine. Recommendation skips boards below MA20 or with an empty bound book. Tracking a researched board opens Sector Pick; boards without a recipe stay on this tape and never enter Monitor.

sectorPick.title: Sector Pick
sectorPick.subtitle: Among researched optimal backtests, rank which board the current tape favors (the map). The execution theme stays locked while its book is healthy; it does not rotate just because another board is rank 1. Switch only on a leftover book, or after a challenger leads for consecutive days with a real score gap. Boards with a leftover strategy book (fewer than 3 names, or one name above 50%) cannot become the lock.
sectorPick.emptyHero: Tick the boards to include, then Scan now. A full scan can take a while.
sectorPick.holdingsHint: Target weights from the winning board’s signal engine (not a broker account). Pick a date to replay that day’s pick; same-day scans overwrite that day’s snapshot.
sectorPick.emptyHoldings: No holdings yet. Scan to load the recommended board’s book.
sectorPick.historyHint: Pick a date to replay that day’s recommended board and holdings. Same-day rescans keep only the latest pass.
sectorPick.chartHint: Top: rank (1 at the top). Bottom: 20-day momentum. Click a date to replay that scan. Hover a legend name or a line to highlight both charts and show that board only; click the legend to hide a board.
sectorPick.chartNeedMore: Only one snapshot so far — points are that day’s ranks. Scan more dates to see the path.
sectorPick.tableHint: All researched boards are included by default. Uncheck, save, then scan to drop them. Grey text is the Monitor strategy title. The highlighted row is the locked theme (the order); rank 1 is only the observation map. Residual-book rows stay ranked but cannot become the lock.
sectorPick.bookResidualHint: Too few holdings or one name above 50% — index may still lead, but this board is not recommended.
sectorPick.provisionalHint: Uses live price as today’s close proxy; may flip after the official close.
sectorPick.hintLock: The execution theme. A healthy book is not replaced just because another board is rank 1.
sectorPick.hintMap: Highest live score today. To replace the lock, the locked book must fail, or this board must lead for consecutive days with a real score gap.
sectorPick.hintChallenger: A sesame must stay map #1 and clearly ahead before it replaces the watermelon. Same-day rescans count as one day.
sectorPick.disclaimer: Research / backtest only — not investment advice. Confirm legs were searched in-sample and may overfit.

process.hintActionWait: Do not buy new names today. Existing holdings may stay or be reduced by later gates. This is not a flatten, and not a bear-market call. Most sessions should look like this.
process.hintActionHold: Keep what you already own; do not add. This is not a green light to buy a full book.
process.hintActionEnter: New names may be opened at the clipped target weights. Exchange rules (limit-up, T+1) still apply; this is not a broker order.
process.hintActionAdd: You may add a little to names you already hold, without exceeding the mandate NAV cap.
process.hintActionTrim: Reduce existing size; do not open new risk. Typical when structure says sell-rally or reduce.
process.hintActionExit: This book should go to zero today. It does not mean open a short.
process.hintSizeNav: How much of account net value this theme may occupy after caps. A ceiling, not a leverage target. 0% means no new buys today — not a broker flatten, not a bear-market call.
process.sizeNavZeroNote: 0% means: do not buy new names in this theme today. Not a broker flatten, and not a bear-market call.
process.sizeNavZeroNotBear: “Soft-bear” is about whether to add. It does not mean the market has entered a bear market.
process.hintVetoGeneric: This layer closed adding/buying. Later opinions cannot reopen it. Tag: {{veto}}
process.hintVetoBear: CSI 300 medium is soft-bear: new theme buys fight a down-stacked tape. Rankings remain visible, not tradable. Not a two-day dip, not a bear-market verdict.
process.hintVetoProvisional: Intraday prices are a proxy close. Using them as the official decision splits live guidance from the backtest.
process.hintVetoIndexBull: An index uptrend did not historically lift this book, so it is not a reason to add.
process.hintVetoIndexBear: Bounces in an index bear are sell windows, not new uptrends.
process.hintVetoFade: The book is mostly expensive or down-trending; new buys would be chasing.
process.hintVetoF0None: Sector timing, confirm coverage, or the leftover-book gate gave no entry right.
process.hintVetoHalf: Eligibility is half/watch: you may hold, not size up. Do not read it as ‘buy full’.
process.hintVetoAnalog: Similar 20-day shapes more often fell over the next 10 sessions. Analog may only block new buys, never create them.
process.hintVetoSize: Earlier gates already set tradable size to 0, so weights are cleared to avoid a fake ‘enter’.
process.hintBlockedNames: The engine wanted to enter these tickers; the process blocked them. Table weights go to 0.
process.hintTrace: Read each gate top-down: what it considered and why it concluded. Later gates may only tighten.
process.hintOverlays: The three opinions before compose. The official action is above; do not pick the more aggressive sentence from here.
process.hintMandate: Process constitution: max book size, no shorts, whether an intraday bar counts. Numbers are knobs; veto order is not.
process.hintOverlay: An overlay is one computed opinion (eligibility, MA structure, or 10-day analogs). Input, not the order.
process.hintF0: F0 is sector entry rights: equal-weight vs the 20-day average and confirm coverage. Full eligibility is not ‘buy full’.
process.hintAnalog: Find past 20-day shapes like today and see whether the next 10 days more often rose or fell. A scenario band, not a target price.
process.hintStructure: Place price versus the 20/60/120-day averages to call bull, bear, or chop, and whether the name looks cheap or expensive.

alphaZoo.title: Alpha Zoo
alphaZoo.browseDesc: Browse formula-driven cross-sectional signals from Qlib, the Kakushadze 101 set, GTJA 191, the academic anomaly literature, and PIT-safe fundamentals. Click any alpha to read its formula and source code, or run a bench to score the whole zoo on a universe and period.
alphaZoo.noAlphasMatch: No alphas match the current filters.
alphaZoo.scoreZoo: Score a zoo on a universe
alphaZoo.scoreDesc: Computes IC / IR for every alpha in the selected zoo over the chosen universe and period, then bucketizes them as alive / reversed / dead.
alphaZoo.noAlive: No alive factors in this run.
alphaZoo.copiedAliveIds: Copied {{count}} alive factors (ID, IC, IR, theme)
alphaZoo.compareDesc: Benches just the alphas you pick on a universe and period, then ranks them by IC / IR with the gap to the leader — far faster than benching a whole zoo when you only care about a shortlist.
alphaZoo.alphaIdsHint: Separate ids with commas or spaces. Tip: tick alphas in the catalogue and hit "Compare" to prefill this.
alphaZoo.enterAtLeast2: Enter at least 2 distinct alpha ids to compare.
alphaZoo.icPositiveTitle: Share of periods with positive IC
alphaZoo.predictiveHalfLifeTitle: Predictive half-life: trading days before the signal's edge decays

zooCardDesc.qlib158: Microsoft Qlib's full 158-feature library covering momentum, volatility, volume and rolling statistical signals.
zooCardDesc.alpha101: The 101 formulaic alphas from Kakushadze (2015); short-horizon cross-sectional signals.
zooCardDesc.gtja191: Guotai Junan Securities' 191 alphas; technical and microstructure signals tuned to China A-share markets.
zooCardDesc.academic: Curated long-horizon anomalies from the academic literature (value, momentum, quality, low-vol, etc.).

home.title: AI-Powered Quant Strategy Research
home.subtitle: Describe a trading strategy in natural language. The agent generates code, runs backtests, and optimizes — all in real time.
home.featureAgentDesc: Natural language strategy generation with ReAct reasoning
home.featureBacktestDesc: Multiple data sources covering A-shares quantitative analysis
home.featureStreamingDesc: Watch the agent think, call tools, and iterate
home.featureReplayDesc: Trade journal analyzer + Shadow Account — extract your rules, backtest them, attribute PnL delta
home.step1Desc: Tell the agent what you want to test, in plain language — no code required.
home.step2Desc: The agent plans, pulls market data, and runs the backtest live, so you can follow every step.
home.step3Desc: See performance metrics, the equity curve, and exportable Pine Script for the strategy.
home.step4Desc: Optionally approve a trading mandate with explicit limits — nothing trades without your confirmation.
